clue.text: Pole inclined to be formal

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for the South Pole
something inclined is tilted, leaning at an angle

explanation.surface: A Polish person tends towards stiff formality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person or a stick; it is just S, the South Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilted speech or manners are stiff and artificially formal.

clue.text: Small change Rex required in a jacket

parts.note: pence are small change, loose coins
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king needs some loose coins put in his jacket pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: A spencer is a short close-fitting jacket, named after an Earl Spencer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spencer is a short double-breasted coat or waist-length garment of the Regency era.

clue.text: Trumped in error-—so unwise

indicators.note: the letters are taken in error, scrambled into a wrong order

explanation.surface: A card player trumped by mistake, which was foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is part of the fodder TRUMPED IN; 'error' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent behaviour lacks caution and good judgement, so it is foolish.

clue.text: Taking the pink paper?

parts.note: taken as written
the Financial Times, FT, is printed on distinctive pink paper

explanation.surface: Someone helps themselves to the salmon-coloured newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times is a British business daily famous for its pink pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is the act of taking something that belongs to another person.

clue.text: Abandon land which is too dry to raise crops

definitions.text: land which is too dry to raise crops

explanation.surface: Farmers leave arid land that will grow nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to forsake or leave behind; a desert is an arid region where little grows.

clue.text: Set in motion first set-back

parts.note: a star is the top performer, the one who comes first

indicators.note: back says the word for set is turned round

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: An early setback in getting something going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-back' hides two pieces: PUT (set) turned round by 'back' gives TUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To start up an engine or venture is to get it going.

clue.text: Carries colours all round America

indicators.note: the colour word wraps all round the short form for America

parts.note: stains are dyes that colour wood or fabric
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: A flag carries its colours around the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain a weight is to bear or support it.

clue.text: Ardour that can turn into mania

indicators.note: turn says these letters change round into a new order

explanation.surface: Enthusiasm that can tip over into frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' works on INTO MANIA as its fodder, though the surface reads it as ardour turning into mania.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation is liveliness and spirit, a synonym for ardour or zest.

clue.text: Drink — put some of the best on ice

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pour a little of the finest over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Drink — put' included 'put', which is only a link: the drink is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a mixer, a fizzy quinine soft drink.

clue.text: He's scrutinised 'by an employer

parts.note: per is Latin for by, as in per post
a user is one who employs or makes use of something

explanation.surface: A worker has been inspected by the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employer' looks like a boss, but here means one who employs, that is uses, a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A peruser is someone who reads or examines something carefully.

clue.text: Out of jam, say

parts.note: ex means out of or from, as in ex-works
to jam into a space is to press or squeeze

explanation.surface: Run out of jam, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' but is the definition: to express is to say.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a thought is to put it into words, to state it.

clue.text: Turner, a delinquent pocketing cash

indicators.note: pocketing says the wrongdoer word holds the coin inside

parts.note: a sinner is a wrongdoer
P is a penny, a coin of cash

explanation.surface: A bent cricketer, a crook taking money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' is not the painter: in cricket a spinner turns the ball off the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinner is a bowler, or a thing, that makes something rotate or turn.

clue.text: Where shoppers at the garden centre can weigh offsets?

definitions.text: Where shoppers at the garden centre can weigh

explanation.surface: Garden-centre shoppers weigh produce on the scales at the till.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words for the first sense: scales sitting on a shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop scales on a till top let customers weigh goods; offsets are weights that balance one force against another.

clue.text: Cut expenses, not for the first time, but still smoked

parts.note: re means again, so not for the first time
to eke out funds is to economise, making money last

explanation.surface: Someone economised again, yet still had a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoked' means gave off smoke or a strong smell, not puffed a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that reeked gave off smoke, fumes or a strong stench.

clue.text: A look-out man

parts.note: read as a man who looks outward, toward other people, rather than a sentry

explanation.surface: A sentry keeping watch.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing, sociable person has attention turned to the world outside rather than inward.

clue.text: Popular nurse she swears!

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a sister is a senior nurse in British hospitals

explanation.surface: A well-liked nurse uses bad language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swears' suggests cursing, but means insists firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: One who insists on something firmly declares it true, as if under oath.

clue.text: Giving up running? It appears in doubt

indicators.note: letters in doubt are unsettled, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A runner wondering whether to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of RUNNING plus IT, signalled by 'in doubt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning in can mean surrendering, handing oneself over to the police.

clue.text: Note the girl's holding up tip and cheer

parts.note: G is a musical note

indicators.note: holding says the girl word has the other piece inside

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: the tip of something is its end

explanation.surface: A girl's tip and a cheerful note.
explanation.walkthrough: END (tip) turned by 'up' gives DNE, held inside LASS after G.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladness is joy or happiness, a synonym for cheer as a state of mind.

clue.text: A short assertion that one's quite unconcerned

explanation.surface: Reassurance that one doesn't mind in the least.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NOT A TALL, someone short; joined, the phrase is a polite 'I don't mind'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short person is the opposite of a tall one; the phrase also politely says no trouble was taken.

clue.text: Falls back repeatedly on the big guns

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second
back says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: again means once more, repeatedly
RA is the Royal Artillery, the big guns

explanation.surface: Artillery repeatedly falls back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' reads as a verb of retreat; it is the noun, waterfalls.
explanation.definitionFit: The great waterfalls on the US-Canada border are the most famous falls in North America.

clue.text: The new warden's name

indicators.note: new says the word is made anew, its letters rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: The new prison warden's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew is a boy's name, that of the patron saint of Scotland.

clue.text: Lorry-driver who's left in some conflict

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: a war is a conflict
gone means having left or departed

explanation.surface: A trucker who deserted during a war.
explanation.walkthrough: A wagon is old-fashioned for a lorry or cart, so a wagoner drives one.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagoner drives a wagon, a goods vehicle like a lorry.

clue.text: A way an engineer can obtain a position

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
CE is a civil engineer

explanation.surface: An engineer finds himself a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a posture or a stated position on an issue.

clue.text: This makes for a better atmosphere generally

definitions.text: This makes for a better atmosphere generally

parts.words: This makes for a better atmosphere generally
parts.note: read literally, a device improving the air in a room, not a mood

explanation.surface: Something that improves the mood all round.
explanation.definitionFit: A system that cools and cleans indoor air makes the air in a building pleasanter.

clue.text: A revolting individual, having the right, is presented to the reigning monarch

parts.note: R is short for right
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the reigning Queen when this was set

explanation.surface: A rebel with rights is brought before the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' means rebelling, not disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: A riser is one who rises up in revolt.

clue.text: Light-weight, but a real beast

explanation.surface: A small weight, yet a fierce animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small unit of weight; it is also the snow leopard.

clue.text: A good man before going after gold, that's plain

indicators.note: going after puts the saint and before pieces after the gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
St is a saint, a good man
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A virtuous man prefers simplicity to gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means severely simple, with no ornament.

clue.text: Shape twelve without a mount

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the time wraps the horse

parts.note: noon is twelve o'clock
a nag is a horse, something to ride

explanation.surface: A dozen people lacking a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonagon is a polygon with nine sides, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Lends a certain sparkle

parts.note: read literally, putting bubbles into a drink rather than wit into a party

explanation.surface: Someone livens up the conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging a liquid with gas makes it fizzy and bubbly.

clue.text: The Spanish are no twisters, the old queen found

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: twisters says the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Spaniards are not liars, the queen discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleanor of Aquitaine, or Eleanor of Castile, were medieval English queens.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor of Aquitaine was a twelfth-century queen of England and France.
